hero.subtitle: A compact, URL-safe token format for securely transmitting claims between parties, the backbone of modern API authentication.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
JSON Web Token (JWT) is a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties. The claims are encoded as a JSON object that is used as the payload of a JSON Web Signature (JWS) structure or as the plaintext of a JSON Web Encryption (JWE) structure.

JWTs are ubiquitous in modern web development. They're used for authentication tokens, API keys, single sign-on, and information exchange between microservices.

sections.title: JWT Structure
sections.content:
A JWT is composed of three parts separated by dots: Header, Payload, and Signature.

JWT Structure
HEADER.PAYLOAD.SIGNATURE

Base64URL(Header) + "." +
Base64URL(Payload) + "." +
Base64URL(Signature)
HeaderJSON object specifying the algorithm (alg) and token type (typ)
PayloadJSON object containing the claims (sub, iss, exp, iat, etc.)
SignatureHMAC or RSA signature over Header + Payload

sections.title: JWT Claims
sections.content:
Claims are statements about an entity (typically the user) and additional data. There are registered, public, and private claims.

issIssuer - who created the token
subSubject - who the token is about
audAudience - intended recipient
expExpiration time (Unix timestamp)
iatIssued at time
nbfNot before time
jtiJWT ID - unique identifier for the token

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Always Verify Signatures
Never trust a JWT without verifying its signature. Use the "alg" header to determine which algorithm to use for verification.
Avoid "alg: none"
The "none" algorithm must be rejected unless explicitly expected. It has been the source of critical vulnerabilities.
Use Short Expiration
JWTs cannot be revoked once issued. Keep expiration times short and use refresh tokens for long sessions.
Don't Store Secrets in Payload
JWT payloads are only Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted. Anyone can read the claims.
